metrics.method: Manual read of all 142 non-service messages in data/chats/kaitlynn-x-altr.jsonl, full history 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-10 (68 from Kaitlynn, 74 from ALTR; 10 service events excluded). Client questions = direct asks, instructions or complaints requiring a response, including the day-one brief, the voice-memo offer, the AM question, the call request, the posting-cadence request, the invoicing-cadence question, the reels-Drive scope question, the wire-friction report, the revenue-drop complaint, the chatter-rotation request, the screenshot request, the two 30-reels questions, the IG flagging disclosure, the Drive failure, the nude-preview breach, the new-content-to-schedule note and the termination message. Unanswered >24h = Aug 19 drop (35d), voice memo (35d), posting cadence (28d), invoicing cadence (25d), wire friction (19d), IG flagging (14d), freeloader screenshots (13d), which Instagram the quota feeds (12d), Drive fix confirmation (9d), and 'lots of new content to schedule / sell / mass' (never acknowledged). The nude-preview breach is excluded from this count because it drew a reply in 3 minutes — it failed on resolution, not response. Max team silence = last ALTR message 2026-08-21 18:53 to next 2026-08-27 17:14 = 5.93 days, ended by us asking her a question. Promises = explicit forward commitments by our side; kept 6 (wall-post Drive delivered, custom domain delivered, 'answer shortly' on the revenue drop delivered in 18h, meeting link within 30 min on 9/4, final invoice in ~10h, payment link in 37 min); lapsed 9 (book the 8/14 call, 'posted consistently across your management IG account', the $91 waiver, 'I'll let you know soon' on the IG account, Mica's weekly creative ideas, Mica's 'i'll check back in!', Derrek's Drive fix, the DM content handoff never confirmed back to the group, 'Will look into this now' on the breach).

what_client_wanted: A working way to pay us — 'I need the final invoice and an alternative way to make payments immediately since I cannot wire' (9/8), first flagged as 'Had to jump through a few hoops with the wire transfer. Not sure why.' (8/21). It is the only priority that appears inside her termination message.

Aggressive selling with a girlfriend-experience style, and chatters who never give content away — 'please sell the f*uck out of content, don’t be afraid to be aggressive with selling or pricing, and always be like a gf to them' (8/7) and 'chat team is not allowed to send free full nude previews' (9/4).

A consistent, dedicated chatter rotation and an explanation of her revenue swings — 'would love to keep a consistent rotation of the same chatters on my profile. Instead of throwing in multiple different people who don’t really know my account' (8/28).

Realistic, personalised social strategy and voice contact rather than boilerplate — 'I’m probably not gonna be the creator that’s gonna post every single day' (8/31) and 'Would love to hop on a call with someone just to discuss a few things' (8/14), re-asked 9/4.
what_worked: Speed, when anyone actually applied it. Mayson replied to her re-asked call request in 34 seconds and had a meeting link up within 30 minutes (9/4) — proof the preceding three weeks of delay were oversight, not capacity. The same pattern produced the payment link in 37 minutes on 9/9.

Real numbers, delivered over a weekend. Ollie answered the revenue-drop complaint inside 18 hours with screenshots on 8/29 — the only performance report ever posted on this account, and the shape of thing she kept asking for.

Personalised outreach converts where self-serve links do not. Twenty days of a cold Calendly converted nothing; Mica's one tailored message on 8/31 — 'that’s also why I wanted to have an initial call with you so I could get to know you better, understand your goals and what’s realistic for you' — converted in six minutes: 'Scheduled for 2pm Wednesday :)'. She was also unusually generous with praise when we delivered: 'I am really impressed and thankful for the numbers and efforts in the account' (8/17).
top_fix: Score complaint severity on content, not tone — and give every soft-register complaint a named owner and a 24-hour written answer. Every item that killed this account was reported politely and therefore treated as optional: 'Had to jump through a few hoops with the wire transfer. Not sure why.' (8/21) was answered with silence and became the wire rejection that terminated the engagement 18 days later; 'polite side note: chat team is not allowed to send free full nude previews' got three minutes of attention and then nothing. Bolt two mechanisms onto it: a day-14 onboarding close-out where one named owner reads the client's day-one brief back to her and closes or explicitly drops every item in it, and an alert that routes any credential change on a managed account to the owner within the hour — we saw her lock us out on 9/7 and let the signal die in a group chat 19 hours before she quit.
